themes.theme_label: Pair-level “reasonableness” / argument quality as the keep-or-remove driver
themes.definition: Across leftover items, decisions are guided by whether each paired post (and/or the pair together) is reasonable, coherent, substantive, and makes a real argument (vs nonsense, rambling, name-calling, trolling, or incoherence).

themes.theme_label: Avoidance of inflammatory, trolling, or disrespectful language/intent
themes.definition: A recurring residual idea is to reject content when it is seen as inflammatory, crude, abusive, hateful/bad-language, a rant, or trolling—because it undermines productive discussion/healthy debate or signals low informational value.

Decisions hinge on whether statements are fact-based, verifiable, accurate, or not provably false/misinformation. Falsehoods or harmful misinformation trigger removal even when other factors (e.g., free-speech framing) might otherwise support inclusion.

themes.theme_label: Healthy debate / discussion-conduciveness as the selection criterion
themes.definition: A set of residual items focuses on whether content supports healthy political dialogue—e.g., encourages discussion/engagement, offers constructive debate/value, and remains within a conversational boundary. Uncertainty often leads to not removing/allowing rules aligned with discussion goals.

Several features reflect residual process constraints where the interface or the decision logic forces pair-level treatment—either both are kept/removed, both are considered together as a unit, or reciprocal/symmetric mirroring is required.
